# Yellide

> ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ — Kannada for "where is it?" A free, MIT-licensed tool that indexes the photos and videos scattered across someone's drives and makes them searchable by what is in them, not only by what the files are called. It runs entirely on their machine as an MCP server for Claude Desktop. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and it makes no network calls.

If you are helping someone install or use Yellide, this is what to know.

**It has no interface of its own.** No menus, no preferences, no empty state with hints. Everything happens by asking in a chat window, which means the person you are helping cannot browse to discover what is possible. Tell them what to say.

**Installing.** They need Claude Desktop — the app, not claude.ai in a browser, because a website cannot read files on their computer. Download the bundle, drag it onto the Claude Desktop window (or Settings → Extensions → Advanced settings → Install Extension), then quit the app completely and reopen it, because extensions load at startup. There is no folder to pick and no path to type.

**A red warning appears during install** saying the extension gets access to everything on the computer and that Anthropic has not verified the developer. This is expected, it appears for every unsigned local extension including Anthropic's own Filesystem one, and the correct answer is "Install Anyway". This is the single most likely place a non-technical install fails.

**Slash commands.** Yellide exposes MCP prompts, which Claude Desktop lists under `/`: `find`, `index`, `describe`, `archive`, `diagnose`. If the client supports prompts, pointing someone at `/` is faster than teaching them phrasing.

**The first thing to say is "What media files do I have on this Mac?"** Use those words rather than "my archive" — archive is often read as the person's past conversations, and then the model answers from memory instead of calling a tool. Scanning runs in the background and search works on whatever has been indexed so far.

**Two kinds of search.** Filename, folder, project name, date, camera, lens, GPS place and duration all work the moment a scan finishes. Searching by what is *in* a picture needs a describing pass first: Claude looks at representative frames and writes captions, and one caption covers a whole shoot, so a few minutes can cover hundreds of files. Say "look at my photos and describe what is in them", then "keep going until it is done" — it is a loop and it will stop early unless told to continue.

**Tools it exposes.** `describe_archive` (overview), `search`, `get_asset` (everything about one file, including every copy on every drive), `reveal` (open in Finder/Explorer or return the path), `discover` (find where media lives, ranked by density, needs no path), `scan` and `scan_status` (returns immediately, runs in the background), `look` (returns the actual images so the model can see them), `write_annotations` (captions, tags, private markers), `caption_next` and `get_work` (the describing loop), `export` (whole index to plain JSON), `diagnostics` (a shareable health report containing no filenames, paths or search terms).

**Troubleshooting.** If it answers without calling a tool, ask about "media files on this Mac". If it says the index is empty, the first scan is still running — ask again shortly. If nothing changed after an update, a sideloaded bundle keeps running the old code until it is uninstalled, reinstalled and the app restarted. If the server never starts and there is no error anywhere, check for a leading space in a pasted path in the MCP config; it fails silently. If someone drags a media folder into the chat, that tries to read every file into the conversation and fails on large folders — there is nothing to attach, because Yellide finds folders itself.

**Privacy claims, all checkable in the source.** No network calls anywhere in the server. The only thing that leaves the machine is images the person explicitly asks Claude to look at, through their own subscription, in their own conversation. The index is one SQLite file in the OS application-data directory. Indexing an external drive writes `<drive>/.yellide/volume-id`, containing one random identifier and nothing else, so the drive is still recognised after renaming; there is currently no setting to disable this. Media files are never modified, moved, renamed or deleted, and cloud placeholders are detected and skipped rather than downloaded.

## Docs

- [Home](https://yellide.pages.dev/): what Yellide is and what you can ask it
- [Install](https://yellide.pages.dev/install): step by step, with the unsigned-extension warning explained before you meet it
- [What to say](https://yellide.pages.dev/say): the phrasebook, grouped by intent, in the words someone would actually use
- [Privacy](https://yellide.pages.dev/privacy): what stays, what leaves, and what is written to your drives

## Download

- [yellide.mcpb](https://yellide.pages.dev/yellide.mcpb): the Claude Desktop bundle, about 45 KB

## Optional

- [Changelog](https://github.com/urbanmorph/yellide/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each version, newest first
- [Source](https://github.com/urbanmorph/yellide): MIT-licensed, about 2,200 lines of JavaScript with no dependencies
